changes.comment: Work over a vault from outside the app: find, read and edit notes through one set of typed operations over the plain files on disk — no relay, no sync, no second copy of anything.

Read the part of a note you actually need — its outline, one section by heading, a line range, or just its frontmatter — instead of the whole thing, with an explicit marker when an answer was cut short.
Every answer says what it was computed over: how many notes, how many files were skipped as binary, and which folders were never looked at — so “nothing found” is never mistaken for “nothing exists”.
Every edit made this way keeps a copy of the previous version first and then writes the file in one atomic step, so a tool’s change can always be undone and a half-written note is never left on disk.
Undo an outside edit with restore: list the versions kept before each write — the app’s own and the command line’s together — and put any of them back.
Ask what changed since a moment in time and pick up where you left off, instead of re-reading the vault.

Edits are refused rather than guessed: replacing text that appears more than once, creating a note that already exists, moving or deleting more than twenty files without confirmation, or writing a note that changed since it was read.
